title: FedNLR: Federated Learning with Neuron-wise Learning Rates

problem.claim: Data heterogeneity among federated learning clients causes severe performance degradation.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally treat the model as a whole and do not deeply analyze how individual neurons evolve during local training to form model drift.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes activation changes of individual neurons during federated local training.
It identifies neuron drift, in which neurons highly activated for a class lose activation when that class is absent from a client's local samples, reducing performance on that class.
It proposes FedNLR, an algorithm that uses neuron-wise learning rates during federated local training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FedNLR as a novel algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that FedNLR achieves state-of-the-art performance for federated learning with popular deep neural networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning suffers performance degradation from client data heterogeneity.
Prior methods attribute the issue to local model drift and calibrate update directions, but generally analyze the model holistically.
The paper analyzes neuron-level activation changes and identifies neuron drift affecting classes absent from local data.
FedNLR applies neuron-wise learning rates to strengthen local-class neurons while preserving non-local class knowledge.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on federated learning with popular deep neural networks.

source_observation.claim: Local training on heterogeneous client data can reduce the activation of neurons associated with classes absent from that client's samples.

interpretation.claim: Model drift may arise from class-specific neuron decay rather than only from aggregate update-direction disagreement.

application.claim: Analyze and control parameter or representation updates at a finer granularity when aggregate model-level correction obscures heterogeneous effects.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether neuron-wise control helps beyond the reported federated learning settings or model architectures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical analysis, datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the exact neuron-wise learning-rate rule or its computational and communication costs.
